resources.string: Per-target UDP 137 · timeout 200 ms · 8 concurrent workers
Querying targets one by one — responding NetBIOS hosts will appear here in real time
No host responded to NBSTAT this run — see the notes below; this is a common result
Enter an IP / subnet, then tap START SCAN

[!] Only devices running Windows with NetBIOS over TCP/IP enabled respond on UDP 137; Windows 10/11 may disable it by default, so few or zero results are normal and do not mean the subnet has no devices.
In responses, <00> is the workstation name, <03> the messenger / logged-in user, <20> the file service and <1D> the master browser; other name types are filtered out.

MAC is taken from the Unit ID in the response statistics; without statistics the system ARP cache is tried (usually unreadable on Android 10+). When neither is available it shows -- and makes no guesses.
Vendor names come from a built-in table of common OUI first-3-byte prefixes; unlisted addresses show \"unknown vendor\". The table is a small offline list, not an authoritative database.
/24 and larger subnets scan only the /24 containing the entered address (1-254); /25-/32 is enumerated over the actual host range.
All results come from real NBSTAT responses; full raw packets are kept in rawHex and can be exported for Wireshark review.
